Title: Plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 is independently associated with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease whereas leptin and adiponectin vary between genders.

Journal/Date: Journal of gastroenterology and hepatology (2015)

MeSH Keywords: Adiponectin, Analysis of Variance, Asian People, Biomarkers, Female, Humans, Leptin, Male


--- ABSTRACT ---
[BACKGROUND AND AIM]: Alterations of adipocytokine levels and clinical parameters in non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) are crucial for the prognosis and complications of the diseases. However, the key adipocytokines independently associated with NAFLD have not been identified, and we aimed to investigate them.
[METHODS]: This study was conducted on a consecutive series of 210 Taiwanese NAFLD patients and 420 sex- and age-matched controls. Fatty liver was diagnosed by magnetic resonance spectroscopy. The enrolled subjects' body mass indexes, homeostasis model of assessment-insulin resistance, uric acid, total cholesterol, triglyceride, high-density lipoprotein, low-density lipoprotein, blood pressure, metabolic syndrome (yes/no), alanine aminotransferase, aspartate aminotransferase-to-platelet ratio indexes, leptin, adiponectin, and plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1) levels were analyzed to determine their association with NAFLD.
[RESULTS]: Univariate analysis showed that all of the aforementioned factors were associated with NAFLD, whereas multivariate analysis revealed that only PAI-1 (odds ratio: 1.39, P = 0.039) was independently associated with NAFLD. Subgroup analysis showed that females consistently had higher leptin (P < 0.001) and adiponectin (P < 0.001) levels than males, whereas their PAI-1 levels were similar. Males with NAFLD had higher leptin but lower adiponectin levels than their subgroup counterparts (all P < 0.001). Among the female subgroups, hyperleptinemia and hypoadiponectinemia were only observed in the NAFLD patients ≥ 45 years.
[CONCLUSIONS]: PAI-1 is independently associated with NAFLD after adjusting for other factors, including leptin and adiponectin. Male and female NAFLD patients show distinct patterns of leptin and adiponectin alterations; special attention is required when evaluating these alterations in female NAFLD patients < 45 years.

key_findings.finding: A Taiwanese case-control study (210 NAFLD, 420 age/sex-matched controls; MRI/MRS-defined fatty liver) found that although BMI, HOMA-IR, lipids, blood pressure, metabolic syndrome, leptin, adiponectin and PAI-1 were associated with NAFLD in univariate analyses, only PAI-1 remained independently associated in multivariable analysis (OR 1.39, P=0.039). This directly supports an obesity/insulin-resistance-adjusted association, although the abstract does not provide the model's full covariate list or CI.

source_tools.relevance: Direct human multivariable study and effect estimate

key_findings.finding: The CARDIA prospective analysis supports temporality and robustness: among 809 initially largely healthy adults, higher PAI-1 in young adulthood was independently associated with CT-defined NAFLD in midlife, with adjusted OR 2.16 per 1-SD higher log PAI-1 (95% CI 1.63-2.85) at the first assessment and 2.71 (95% CI 2.03-3.61) at the second. The available abstract confirms logistic adjustment but does not enumerate all covariates in the displayed text.

Histology-based evidence in 273 predominantly obese biopsy patients found PAI-1 rose with steatosis, lobular inflammation, ballooning and fibrosis; in regression including anthropometric and metabolic parameters, steatosis remained an independent predictor of PAI-1, together with fasting C-peptide and waist circumference explaining 21% of PAI-1 variance. This supports an independent NAFLD-to-PAI-1 relationship but models PAI-1 as the outcome, so it is not equivalent to an independent odds ratio for NAFLD.

source_tools.relevance: Adjusted biopsy/histology analysis and important directionality caveat

key_findings.finding: The combined sex/adipokine claim is supported by the 2015 Taiwanese study: females had higher leptin and adiponectin than males overall (both P<0.001), PAI-1 was similar by sex, and among NAFLD cases males had higher leptin and lower adiponectin than male controls; in females, hyperleptinemia and hypoadiponectinemia were observed only at age ≥45 years. Thus concentrations and NAFLD-associated patterns varied by sex and age.

The overall claim is supported but should be qualified: PAI-1 has human adjusted and prospective evidence for an association with NAFLD beyond measured metabolic confounding, while leptin/adiponectin patterns differ by sex; however, this does not establish that PAI-1 is causally independent, and pediatric evidence shows context-dependent leptin findings (lower leptin associated with steatosis in obese prepubertal children), limiting generalization across age and phenotype.

source_tools.relevance: Context and heterogeneity of leptin association
